routes.reason: Accept. The new roadmap is justified and I re-ran the justification rather than taking it. Searching all 1968 atlas stages returns nothing for 'moduli of curves', 'moduli space of curves', 'tautological ring', 'tautological class', 'Chow ring', 'Borel–Moore', 'Brill–Noether', 'symplectic local system', 'mapping class group', 'psi class', 'kappa class' or 'moduli of stable'. Every near hit dissolves on reading: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry owns general stacks, algebraic spaces and coarse spaces for the generalised elliptic curve and polarised abelian scheme problems, not M̄_{g,n}; StableReduction Layer 9 plans stable pointed curves but not their moduli stack; and the 32 hits for 'gonality' are almost all the substring of 'orthogonality'. So nothing goes in the direction of the cohomology of M̄_{g,n}, and a new roadmap rather than a Part II is right. The brief states the final theorems exactly — Theorem 1.1's three isomorphisms, Theorem 1.3's generator set {H^{k'}(M̄_{g',n'}) : k' ≤ k, g' < (3/2)k' + 1, n' ≤ k', 4g' − 4 + n' ≥ k'}, Theorem 1.5's three parts, Theorems 1.6 and 1.7, Theorem 1.10 — and I checked each against the source, including that `\lstw` is defined as L·S_12. Every stage it names as an import exists and matches the content claimed: StableReduction Layers 1, 3 and 9; HodgeStructures L0, L1 and L2; SF.2, SF.5, MC.0, MC.2, DWP.9, R19.1, R09.1, R09.4 and R09.5. It also flags two inputs as deserving their own layers rather than a citation, which is the right call for the virtual cohomological dimension with Harer stability and for the Bergström–Faber–Payne vanishing. I would build on this.

Accept. SF.5 is 'Intersection theory and Riemann-Roch' and its description does construct Chow groups, rational equivalence, proper pushforward, flat and lci pullback, refined Gysin maps, Chern classes and intersection products, so items 12 and 58 — the Chow groups of algebraic stacks stratified by quotient stacks with excision and the exterior product, and the rational Chow ring of an orthogonal Grassmann bundle — are general facts of that layer rather than facts about moduli of curves. Both stage ids resolve. Note that item 12 routes the *stack* extension of a scheme-level layer here as a source route; that is the right policy, and it is the policy I applied to item 14.

Accept. MC.2 constructs realisation functors and proves cycle classes respect composition, cup products, pushforward, trace and Tate twists, so the cycle class map of item 13 belongs there, and the generality the moduli application needs — a smooth but not necessarily proper variety or Deligne–Mumford stack, landing in the lowest weight part W_{2i}H^{2i} — is the right thing to ask of that layer rather than to re-plan. The item's locator, Lemma 4.3 with Remark 4.4, is correct.

Added by this review, carrying item 14, which I moved from planned to missing. The item asserts Poincaré duality, with the hard Lefschetz injections, for a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack. It was planned at SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 and DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9, but SF.2 is 'Sites and scheme cohomology' and DWP.9 states hard Lefschetz for X projective smooth over an algebraically closed field, so neither plans the stack case, and searching all 1968 stages returns nothing for 'cohomology of a stack', 'duality for stacks' or 'smooth proper Deligne'. The extraction's own note conceded that 'the Deligne–Mumford stack case is used throughout the paper without comment'. Routed to SF.2 as a source route, exactly as items 12 and 13 route the stack extensions of scheme-level layers, with the reason recording that the hard Lefschetz half is DWP.9's obligation and must be stated there for stacks rather than assumed. HodgeStructures L1 supplies polarisation and Hodge–Riemann semisimplicity and is unaffected.
